name: Uganda

findings.summary: Uganda Police contracted Huawei in 2018 for a safe-city CCTV system with facial recognition, reported at $126 million; thousands of cameras feed monitoring centres and a Kampala police data hub, with expansion beyond Kampala planned.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 5: Techpoint (2019) reports about 2,500 of 3,200 planned Kampala cameras installed; Nation (undated, c. late 2022) reports about 5,000 cameras and 11 monitoring centres. $126m is the police-reported figure. Financier: Eagle Online cites a $104m Standard Chartered loan for phases I-II (single source). Phase III ($62m sought in 2025) status unknown.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Internal Affairs / Uganda Police Force
findings.reversal_of: Huawei's maintenance of the Uganda Police safe-city CCTV system
findings.summary: After Huawei came under 2019 sanctions, the Ministry of Internal Affairs moved maintenance of the police CCTV network from Huawei to Ugandan firm Dealan Associates; a 2026 bribery probe over maintenance payments led Museveni to suspend senior officials.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a partial reversal (maintenance/service role only, not removal of Huawei hardware); the handover date is not given. Both sources attribute it to 'US and EU sanctions in 2019'; the EU did not sanction Huawei, so the stated cause is imprecise (sanctions = US Entity List, analyst inference). Whether Huawei still supplies firmware updates is unknown. The 2026 suspensions concern corruption, not the vendor.

findings.summary: MTN Uganda selected Huawei for a five-year project (MUNA) replacing its legacy core network elements with a single-vendor, cloud-native, 5G-capable core, in preparation for 5G; value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Both trade-press reports likely derive from the same operator announcement. MTN Uganda's RAN vendor and Airtel Uganda's vendors were not established; 5G RAN vendor for MTN's 2023 launch not identified.

findings.local_actor: NITA-U / Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
findings.summary: Museveni launched phase V of the National Backbone Infrastructure in December 2024, an Exim Bank of China soft-loan project laying about 5,845 km of fibre to 63 more districts and connecting over 2,800 public sites.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller Huawei rests only on UG Business saying Huawei was the NBI project contractor; NITA does not name a vendor for phase V, so the pole is less certain than the financing. Loan sought after the World Bank paused new lending in 2023; phases 1-3 (from 2006/07) were also Exim-financed. Announced value is UG Business's conversion of CNY 1bn (about $146.7m); The African Mirror says $150m.

findings.summary: Synectics Technologies announced a 100MW renewable-powered data centre and 'digital city' on over 80 acres in Uganda, valued around Ksh157.2 billion, with Schneider Electric, Nvidia and Turner & Townsend as partners and an AI centre of excellence.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the source does not give Synectics Technologies' home jurisdiction or ownership. Tier 1: announcement only, rollout said to begin mid-2026; no evidence of financing or construction. Value in KES not converted. Nvidia named as partner but no accelerator purchase stated, so no silicon finding.

findings.summary: Raxio, a subsidiary of US greenfield investor Roha, planned Uganda's first Tier III colocation data centre at Namanve Industrial Park near Kampala, up to 400 racks and 1.5MW, self-funded by Roha.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us from DCD describing Roha as a US firm; Raxio Group's later ownership (e.g. other investors) was not checked. Tier 2 because the source describes a plan; a PeeringDB listing (not cited, S5) suggests the facility operates, which would make it tier 5. Pre-2020; still_current unconfirmed. Small scale, not AI-specific.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
findings.summary: Sunbird AI's Sunflower, a multilingual model for Ugandan languages, was unveiled by the ICT ministry's permanent secretary in October 2025; Sunbird's model card says Sunflower-14B is built on Qwen3-14B under Apache 2.0.

sources.publisher: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance

findings.analyst_inference: Domestic: Sunbird AI is a Ugandan organisation publishing its own weights. Base model pole prc (Alibaba Qwen). A 32B variant and a Gemma-based variant appeared in search results but were not opened. Tier 2: a ministry launch and partnership, not a documented procurement or government-wide deployment.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or export-licence reporting found; silicon not given a dedicated search, Nvidia only named as a partner in an announced data centre

power.null_reason: no AI-specific power evidence surfaced beyond a 100MW renewable claim in the Synectics announcement

research_gaps: Who supplies MTN Uganda's 5G RAN and Airtel Uganda's RAN and core?
Confirm the NBI phase V equipment vendor/EPC contractor from NITA-U or the Exim loan agreement, and the loan amount approved by Parliament.
When was Huawei's maintenance role on the police CCTV system handed to Dealan Associates, and does Huawei still supply firmware/updates? Status of the $62m phase III request.
Ownership and home jurisdiction of Synectics Technologies; has the 100MW Uganda data centre reached financing or construction?
Current ownership and capacity of Raxio UG1, and any 2023+ data-centre projects (e.g. Africa Data Centres, government data centre presented at the NBI phase V launch).
Does Uganda government use Sunflower operationally, and is there any foreign frontier-model provider partnership with ministries?
